title: Unleashing the Power of T1-cells in SFQ Arithmetic Circuits
problem: Gate-level pipelining in SFQ systems incurs significant area overhead due to path balancing requirements, and this overhead is particularly detrimental given the limited layout density inherent to RSFQ technology.
motivation: RSFQ technology offers orders of magnitude smaller power dissipation than conventional electronics, making it attractive for cloud computing, aerospace electronics, and quantum computing interfaces.
method: T1-cells are specialized circuit building blocks for Rapid Single Flux Quantum (RSFQ, a type of superconducting logic) arithmetic circuits. They reduce the extra circuitry overhead that comes with pipelining—splitting computation into stages so multiple operations run in parallel—which normally requires synchronizing signal timing across different paths. T1-cells achieve this by optimizing the circuit layout to pack components more tightly, a particularly important consideration in RSFQ systems where layout density is limited.
key_novelty: T1-cells are circuit primitives that reduce pipelining overhead in RSFQ arithmetic circuits by enabling tighter component packing.
contributions: T1-cell design for SFQ arithmetic circuits
Reduced area overhead in pipelined SFQ systems
Improved physical layout density for RSFQ implementations
